title: Affine pullbacks of perfect objects detect isomorphisms on algebraic spaces
statement:
Use schemes [def-pc-scheme], algebraic spaces with their small etale structure sheaves [def-trf-algebraic-space], module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], and unbounded derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Write $D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_Z)$ for the full subcategory with quasi-coherent cohomology [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module]. Derived pushforward is computed by K-injective resolutions and tensor pullback $Lh^*$ by K-flat resolutions. Quasi-compact means that every open cover has a finite subcover; quasi-separated means the diagonal is quasi-compact. A perfect complex is etale locally isomorphic to a bounded complex of direct summands of finite free structure-sheaf modules. Let $S$ be a scheme and $h:Z'\to Z$ an affine morphism of quasi-compact quasi-separated algebraic spaces over $S$. Here affine means representable with affine inverse images of affine scheme charts. Let $v:C\to D$ be a morphism in $D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_{Z'})$. If for every perfect $P\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_Z)$ and every integer $j$ postcomposition by $v[j]$ gives a bijection
$$\operatorname{Hom}(Lh^*P,C[j])\longrightarrow\operatorname{Hom}(Lh^*P,D[j]),$$
then $v$ is an isomorphism.

source.place: Tags 09IY (theorem-bondal-van-den-Bergh), 0E4R (remark-pullback-generator), affine case: shifted-Hom zero-cone detection.

proof.text: Choose the perfect weak generator $P$ on $Z$ supplied by [lem-sfb-space-perfect-weak-generator]; its hypotheses hold because $Z$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated. Complete $v$ to a distinguished triangle $C\xrightarrow{v}D\xrightarrow{a}K\xrightarrow{b}C[1]$ in the unbounded module derived category [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. The cone $K$ has quasi-coherent cohomology: [lem-sfb-space-perfect-localizing-generation] explicitly says that $D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}$ is closed under distinguished-triangle cones. Apply that closure to $C,D$ on $Z\prime$.

For every integer $n$, $P[n]$ is perfect, since shifting a bounded finite-projective local representative remains bounded and finite-projective. Put $A=Lh^*(P[n])$. The hypothesis with test object $P[n]$ and $j=0,1$ says that $\operatorname{Hom}(A,v)$ is surjective and $\operatorname{Hom}(A,v[1])$ is injective. We show $\operatorname{Hom}(A,K)=0$ using [lem-weil-pbc-hom-into-triangle-exact]. Given $t:A\to K$, the triangle relation gives $v[1]bt=0$; injectivity implies $bt=0$. Exactness in the rotated triangle yields $t=as$ for some $s:A\to D$. Surjectivity gives $s=vr$ for some $r:A\to C$, whence $t=avr=0$. This holds for every $n$; no boundedness of $C,D,K$ was used.

The derived adjunction $Lh^*\dashv Rh_*$ stated in [lem-sfb-space-derived-etale-chart-calculus] identifies the vanishing just obtained with $\operatorname{Hom}(P[n],Rh_*K)=0$ for every $n$. By [lem-sfb-space-affine-derived-pushforward-conservative], $Rh_*K$ has quasi-coherent cohomology. The zero-detection clause of [lem-sfb-space-perfect-weak-generator] therefore gives $Rh_*K\cong0$. Apply affine conservativity to the zero endomorphism $0:K\to K$: its image is an isomorphism between zero objects, so $0:K\to K$ is an isomorphism. Its inverse identity implies $\mathrm{id}_K=0$, hence $K\cong0$.

With $K\cong0$, exactness for the triangle and its rotation [lem-weil-pbc-hom-into-triangle-exact] makes $\operatorname{Hom}(W,v)$ bijective for every $W$: existence follows from $\operatorname{Hom}(W,K)=0$, and uniqueness from $\operatorname{Hom}(W,K[-1])=0$. For $W=D$ choose $r:D\to C$ with $vr=\mathrm{id}_D$. For $W=C$, injectivity and $v(rv)=v$ give $rv=\mathrm{id}_C$. Thus $r$ is an inverse of $v$, as required.
